.DISCUSSION...

KEY MESSAGE 1...Cooler and drier conditions are forecast for Saturday, 
before showers and thunderstorms return Sunday.

Cdfnt will continue to push south of the area this afternoon
with isolated light showers ending from north to south, but
could linger through mid evening in central VA. Surface ridging
builds in for Saturday supporting fair weather conditions. Warm
air and moisture advection atop a shallow cool layer will
support scattered showers across the northern half of the fcst
area late Sat night into Sunday. Then, additional showers and
thunderstorms are expected Sunday afternoon and evening along a
retreating warm front. The front will sink south Sunday night as
low pressure passes by and high pressure starts building south
again. 


KEY MESSAGE 2...Daily chances for showers persists into next week 
along with cooler temperatures. 

Upper-level ridging breaks down early next week, with multiple 
shortwave disurbances moving across the Mid-Atlantic in the days 
following. Mid-level moisture brought in from the south will 
continue overhead as winds flow northeasterly. As a result, daily 
showers remain a possibility into late next week as these 
disturbances slowly track across the region. Temperatures drop 
on Tuesday in the wake of one of these disturbances, with highs 
generally ranging in the upper 50s and 60s. This cooler- than- 
average weather persists at least through midweek as nearby 
disturbances continue to bring rain showers to the area. Towards
the bay & coastlines, wind gusts could remain elevated mid-to- 
late week as these disturbances begin to track offshore. 
Overall, coastal flooding could become something to watch out 
for next week as these elevated winds combined with persistent 
rain stretches on. 

&&

.AVIATION /18Z FRIDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...

Clouds expected to hang around tonight into Sat morning, but
cigs should remain VFR. Clearing is expected Sat afternoon,
before low clouds redevelop again toward Sunday morning. Low
clouds/overcask skies will remain prevalent early next week. 

Winds generally flow north to northeasterly between Tuesday and 
Wednesday. Showers and thunderstorms are possible each day, 
potentially bringing intermittent sub-VFR conditions across most 
terminals. Wind gusts gradually increase as the week continues.

&&

.MARINE...

SCAs were issued for late tonight into Sat morning as winds
strengthen behind a northerly surge. Winds diminish Sat
afternoon, but pick up again across the southern waters on
easterly flow. 

Winds begin to increase starting Monday afternoon and could 
potentially approach gale conditions between Tuesday night and 
Wednesday as a trough lingers near the waters. Showers & possibly a 
few thunderstorms are possible during this period as the trough 
slowly moves out of the region. Depending on how slowly the trough 
tracks, winds could stay elevated into late next week. Winds 
generally flow northeasterly.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...

As onshore flow strengthens next week, expect water levels to
rise each day with minor coastal flooding becoming likely on
Monday and possibly reaching moderate category by mid next week.
